market_implied_expectations: At the pool-verified $106.79 price, the reverse DCF requires 16.35% annual strict free-cash-flow growth for 4.5 years, from $629.9m LTM to about $1,245.1m in FY2030, if the model's 6.2168% WACC and 0.80% terminal growth are held fixed; that is a 19.21% FY2030 FCF margin on the DCF revenue path. Alternatively, holding the engine's explicit cash path fixed reconciles the price at a 5.0466% market-implied WACC. These explanations are non-exclusive and model-conditional; the price does not establish either one by itself. [analyses/AKAM_2026-09-14/valuation/05_reverse-dcf.md, sections 2-5]
engine_view: The published base case uses consensus revenue of $4,491.3m / $5,078.7m / $5,662.3m in FY2026-FY2028, followed by analyst growth of 8.0% and 6.0% in FY2029-FY2030; GAAP EBIT margin recovers from 10.5% to 14.0%, CFO margin from 30.0% to 33.5%, and cash capex falls from 20.0% to 18.5% of revenue. Full-year strict FCF is $449.1m / $558.7m / $707.8m / $856.1m / $972.3m. The final decision is Avoid with 50/100 stated conviction, a 5-point integrity haircut, and 45/100 post-review confidence. what_everyone_knows: Security and Cloud Infrastructure Services are growing while legacy Delivery is shrinking: Q2 FY2026 Security grew 10%, CIS grew 39%, and Delivery and other cloud applications fell 6%. Management has described more than $2.8bn of signed 2026 multi-year CIS commitments and expects more conversion in Q4 2026 and Q1 2027. Capital IQ's recommendation is Outperform and its 23 target prices average $153.31. These are public consensus and management-narrative facts, not an edge. [analyses/AKAM_2026-09-14/final_thesis.md, sections 4, 5, 9A and 17]
what_is_priced_in: The defensible priced-in statement is conditional: $106.79 needs either materially more cash than the engine's base path—16.35% annual FCF growth to $1,245.1m by FY2030 at a 6.2168% WACC—or a lower required return of about 5.05% on the engine's existing cash path. Consensus targets show optimism, but target prices are analyst opinions and are not independent proof of the market's embedded operating assumptions. [analyses/AKAM_2026-09-14/valuation/05_reverse-dcf.md, sections 2-5; analyses/AKAM_2026-09-14/valuation/99_valuation-synthesis.md, sections 1-3]
what_market_may_be_missing: Revenue mix improvement may not equal economic value creation. Q2 revenue rose 5.4%, yet GAAP gross margin fell 331 basis points and GAAP-derived EBITDA fell 18.7%; LTM strict FCF was $629.9m, 9.92% below FY2025. Security and CIS category profit, capital, and cash conversion are undisclosed, strict net leverage is 5.14x, and $2.066bn of FY2021-FY2025 cash acquisitions plus $205m for LayerX lack a filed deal-level return scorecard. The possible miss is that investors may be capitalizing category revenue growth before it becomes durable group cash flow. [analyses/AKAM_2026-09-14/final_thesis.md, sections 4-6 and 9b; analyses/AKAM_2026-09-14/valuation/05_reverse-dcf.md, section 3]
evidence_engine_is_different: The conclusion is visibly different from target-price consensus: the engine's published $68.78 base value is 35.59% below the market price, while the $153.31 mean target is 43.56% above it. Filing-backed evidence supports the concern—Q2 gross margin fell 331 basis points, GAAP-derived EBITDA fell 18.7%, and the matched FCF record is far below the conditional 16.35% price-implied growth path. But these are public observations, no matched consensus FCF or category-margin series proves investors underweight them, and the proposed $733m LTM FCF threshold for Q2 FY2027 is a prospective falsification test rather than present proof of informational difference. There is no proven variant perception yet. [analyses/AKAM_2026-09-14/final_thesis.md, sections 4, 10 and 17; analyses/AKAM_2026-09-14/valuation/05_reverse-dcf.md, sections 2-5]
base_rate_check: The reverse-DCF requirement is tested against the same group-level strict-FCF metric: FCF was $618.4m in FY2023, $833.9m in FY2024, $699.3m in FY2025, and $629.9m LTM, giving 6.34% FY2023-FY2025 CAGR followed by a 9.92% LTM decline, versus 16.35% annual growth required at the model WACC. That is the right metric and level, but only three annual observations plus one derived LTM period, so it is judgment informed by a short sample, not an empirical frequency. The Security/CIS mix shift could make consolidated history a weak guide, but category cash economics are unavailable. The engine's caution respects the observed base rate; it does not prove the market is wrong or that the gap will close. [analyses/AKAM_2026-09-14/valuation/05_reverse-dcf.md, sections 3-5]
